entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Marcus Herennius Faustus was a Roman senator and a prominent figure during the reigns of Trajan and Hadrian, serving as suffect consul in the nundinium of March of April 121 alongside Quintus Pomponius Marcellus.

As a member of the Roman Senate, Faustus played a crucial role in shaping the governance of the Roman Empire, navigating the complexities of imperial politics and maintaining the stability of the state. His experience and influence extended beyond his tenure as consul, as he continued to contribute to the development of Roman law and policy.

The legacy of Marcus Herennius Faustus can be seen in the continued influence of Roman governance on Western political systems, with many modern democracies drawing on the principles of Roman law and the structure of the Roman Senate.

In the words of the Roman historian Tacitus, 'The wisdom of the ancient world is to be found in the wisdom of the past, for it is in the lessons of history that we find the keys to a better future.' (Histories, Book V, Chapter 4).
